sections.label: The practice
sections.statement: The rigour of a great hotel company, <t>at the scale of each property.</t>
body: Thirty-five years inside IHCL, the company behind the Taj: from a duty manager’s desk at St. James’ Court in London, through fifteen years in Business Excellence, to helping build and scale amã Stays & Trails into a distinctive hospitality brand.
Today, an independent advisory practice for owners of homestays and hotels, for groups in growth, and for the boards that guide them.
sections.sign: अतिथि देवो भव · the guest is god

sections.label: Engagements
sections.title: Where the work <t>usually begins.</t>
items: A family home that could welcome guests, but has never been run as a business.
A beautiful property whose guests do not come back.
A team that serves well on good days, and only on good days.
A group that is growing faster than its standards.
A new hotel or homestay, still on paper, that needs an operator’s eye before it opens.
A board or founder who wants someone at the table who has run hotels.

sections.label: Convictions
sections.title: Eight convictions, <t>on the record.</t>

items.t: A complaint is a gift.
items.q: “Every time a guest has complained and been not so polite to me, it was a learning: what we had to correct and what we did wrong.”

items.t: Improvement is not spending.
Data before instinct.
items.q: “If you’re not working with data… that’s more of a dictatorship.”

items.t: Luxury is what your guest says it is.
items.q: “What luxury means to your customer will come from data.”

items.t: Good to great touches the heart.
items.q: “I was in a business, not in a charity. Good to great really happens when you do something that touches somebody’s heart.”

items.t: Respect yourself first.
items.q: “If you have to respect others, you’ve got to first respect yourself.”

items.t: Hire for attitude.
items.q: “We don’t hire for skill, we hire for attitude.”

items.t: Stay relevant.
items.q: “Reinvention is the name of the game.”

sections.src: Transcribed from HospeTalk, episode 35, and Inspire Someone Today, episode 180.

items.k: What can you do to make the wrong become better?

items.t: Today’s Indian traveller is often more travelled than the foreign guest, and expects the real thing: a Mexican dish had better be Mexican.
Ready to spend on a unique experience, not just on a name. Indian hotels now compete for the Indian guest.
A more demanding guest means young front-line teams need the confidence, and the backing, to draw a line.
